summary: WP-003 PASS. Renderer refactoring is clean, correct, and maintainable.

createSortAnchor() in BaseGridRenderer: $sorting local variable correctly eliminates the double call to $this->grid->sorting(). Logic is clean — extraClasses applied via addClasses() only when non-empty, and the sort indicator span wraps a hardcoded UTF-8 character (no XSS risk).

Bootstrap5Renderer override: array_merge() prepends the 5 Bootstrap framework classes before any caller-supplied $extraClasses. Ordering is conventional and consistent. The override delegates entirely to parent::createSortAnchor(), following a minimal delegation pattern with no duplicated logic.
createHeaderCell() correctly calls createSortAnchor($column) without extra classes, preserving the default empty-array path. The hook point is clean.
All 5 acceptance criteria confirmed met. 78/78 tests pass, 0 PHPStan errors.

Non-blocking: The sort direction indicator (<span> with ▲▼) has no aria-hidden attribute. Screen readers will announce the raw Unicode triangle name. Pre-existing UX issue — not introduced by this WP, but worth addressing in a future accessibility pass.

comments.note: Sort direction indicator in BaseGridRenderer::createSortAnchor() uses a <span> with ▲/▼ Unicode characters but has no aria-hidden="true" attribute. Screen readers will announce the raw glyph name ('black up-pointing triangle'). Non-blocking for this WP — pre-existing pattern — but should be addressed in a future accessibility pass.

Bootstrap5Renderer::createSortAnchor() always prepends its 5 framework classes via array_merge. If a subclass of Bootstrap5Renderer passes any of those same classes in $extraClasses, they will be duplicated in the output. Low-risk in practice since consumers should not pass Bootstrap internals, but worth a note for future subclassers.
